newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Central Bank treasurer Edeza resigns.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Central Bank treasurer Edeza resigns.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza said on Thursday he had submitted his resignation and was leaving his post on June 30.
He told Reuters Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson had accepted his resignation but Singson would neither confirm nor denied such a move.
Edeza denied rumours that he was set to join as treasury head Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co Inc, the country's biggest commercial bank.
Central Bank officials are prohibited to join any bank or financial institution within one year after resignation.

Edeza, who became Central Bank treasurer since July 1994, said he intends to take "a much needed rest" in the United States and work on his enrollment next year in Harvard University for a public policy and administration course.
Edeza also denied a rumour that he resigned because of a growing rift with Singson.
"We have a very good rapport with each other. He is a boss who has been very supportive of me," Edeza said.
Central Bank deputy treasurer Eileen Bautista is being eyed as his successor.
"They should not expect any major change when I am gone. There will be no major departure in policy," Edeza said.
Edeza has been a Central Bank trader since 1981.
